A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedNGDB study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title and publication format.

before.justification: v3 reports original retrieval experiments on three knowledge graphs, including HR@3 and MRR results, client-level analyses, convergence measurements, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original FedNGDB experiments and reports additional Central comparisons and more detailed results for the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.1.1 adds L-infinity clipping and zero-mean Laplacian noise to local gradients for local differential privacy. This is an additional protection step beyond v3's secret aggregation; the encoders, aggregation equations, and distributed retrieval procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use FB15k-237, FB15k, and NELL995 with the same eight query structures and in-graph/cross-graph tasks. The ten-client and relation-overlap scenarios already appear in v3's Appendix C; v4 expands their reported results.

E2.justification: Central is added to the five-client comparison in Table 4 and the ten-client and relation-overlap comparisons in v4 Tables 5–6. The three-client comparator set remains Local, Central, FedE, FedR, and FedNGDB, using the same three base encoders.

E3.justification: v4 specifies gradient clipping at C=0.1 and Laplacian noise scale 0.2 as the default experimental treatment, claiming 1-DP; v3's described training lacks this treatment. Data splits, query sampling, embedding dimension, optimizer, and general evaluation metrics are retained. The PDFs do not establish whether retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1–C.2 expands the existing client-count and relation-overlap analyses with Central comparisons and separate in-graph/cross-graph HR@3 and MRR results. The query-type and individual-client analyses are retained. Convergence analysis moves from Section 5.5 to Appendix C.3 without changing its measurements.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging results across clients is retained; the added differential-privacy probabilities are not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 substantially expands Central comparison results and appendix HR@3/cross-graph entries. The ten-client NELL995 FedNGDB MRR changes from 9.17 to 12.11. Table 4 also swaps dataset/model headers while retaining existing numerical blocks: FedNGDB's in-graph MRR 20.83 belongs to Q2P/FB15k-237 in v3 but GQE/FB15k in v4. This changes reported attribution and cannot be interpreted as a performance gain. Table 3 and convergence measurements are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 adds the claimed privacy-budget bound 2C/lambda, a formal epsilon-DP definition, and an Appendix B.3 post-processing argument that the final ranking preserves epsilon-DP. v3 has no corresponding formal privacy account. Existing graph/query definitions, Equations 1–7, and the key-exchange explanation are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain extending federated graph embeddings to complex query answering, providing privacy-preserving FedNGDB, and constructing a benchmark from three public knowledge graphs. The revised foundation-model framing does not materially change these claims, and the conclusion is substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds discussion of the privacy–utility tradeoff and interprets distributed ranking as preserving local privacy guarantees. Section 5.1.3 newly characterizes Local and Central as lower and upper bounds on information available for training. Existing performance interpretations and applicability assumptions are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access pointer in the abstract and specifies the gradient-clipping threshold and Laplacian noise scale. v3 provides neither disclosure. The previously stated 400-dimensional embeddings and AdamW optimizer remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds focused references, including P-NGDB, recent agentic NGDB work, and sources supporting gradient-leakage protection and differential privacy. The existing positioning around federated complex query answering is retained. Publication updates to previously cited works are bibliographic changes rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, revises portions of the abstract and introduction, adds a section roadmap and acknowledgements, and renames Section 2.2. Convergence discussion moves to Appendix C.3 and corrects v3's erroneous FedC names. Most method and experimental prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a two-column ACM format to a single-column TMLR format. Table 4 is reorganized and appendix result tables are expanded. Figure 4 replaces four separate panels with two grouped comparison plots, changing axes, legends, and average-line displays while retaining the underlying bar values. Its revised caption still incorrectly references panel (c).

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful code-access information, fuller Central comparisons, and clearer paired plots. However, Table 4's changed headers reassign retained scores to different model–dataset pairs, making several comparisons unreliable. The new 1-DP claim also lacks privacy accounting across iterative training in Appendix B.3. These unresolved reliability concerns coexist with documentation and evaluation benefits, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
